title: Modeling English teachers’ behavioral intention to use artificial intelligence in middle schools
extended_summary:
This paper examines why middle school EFL teachers intend to use AI in their teaching, focusing on the combination of technology acceptance factors and teachers’ pedagogical knowledge. The authors address a gap in AI-in-education research by shifting attention from technical system development and student users to K-12 teachers’ perceptions and readiness to adopt AI-supported language learning tools.

The study integrates UTAUT (Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, and Facilitating Conditions) with an AI-specific adaptation of TPACK (AIL-TK, AI-TPK, and AI-TPACK). Using a survey of 470 English teachers in an AI education demonstration district in China, the authors conducted exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to test their hypothesized relationships.

Results showed that teachers were generally positive about AI. Behavioral intention was directly predicted by Performance Expectancy, Social Influence, AIL-TK, and AI-TPACK, while Effort Expectancy and AI-TPK did not directly predict intention. Facilitating Conditions predicted the knowledge constructs, and AI-TPACK was the strongest bridge between teachers’ knowledge and their intention to use AI. The paper concludes that teacher professional development and organizational support are important for fostering AI adoption in middle school EFL teaching.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational survey with EFA/CFA/SEM and a reasonably large sample (n=470), but it does not test an intervention or causal effects. It is informative for acceptance/implementation questions, yet it is not strong efficacy evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports positive perceptions and strong intention to use AI, but it does not measure student outcomes or demonstrate effect sizes on learning. Any impact on K-12 practice is indirect and mainly institutional/implementation-oriented.

interventions.use_case: AI-supported English as a foreign language teaching in middle schools, including speech recognition, semantic analysis, and other language technologies used to support listening, speaking, writing, and reading instruction.

finding.finding_summary: This survey study did not measure student achievement directly; instead it found that middle school EFL teachers reported positive perceptions of AI-supported language learning and strong behavioral intention to use it (BI mean = 4.06, SD = 0.59; n=470). The model showed that Performance Expectancy, Social Influence, AIL-TK, and AI-TPACK significantly predicted Behavioral Intention, while Effort Expectancy did not directly do so.
finding.measure: Teachers’ behavioral intention and perceived usefulness/ease of AI for EFL teaching

finding.finding_summary: Teachers believed AI could improve teaching quality and efficiency, and Performance Expectancy was the strongest predictor of behavioral intention in the SEM. The paper reports that AI was perceived as useful for reducing effort in teaching-related tasks, but it did not provide an intervention effect size for actual workload reduction.
finding.measure: Perceived teaching efficiency and usefulness (Performance Expectancy)

finding.finding_summary: The study found that Facilitating Conditions significantly predicted AIL-TK, AI-TPK, and AI-TPACK, indicating that school and organizational support were associated with stronger teacher readiness to use AI. The authors argue this supports policy and professional development efforts in an AI education demonstration district, but the evidence is correlational rather than causal.
finding.measure: Perceived facilitating conditions, teacher knowledge constructs, and behavioral intention
